Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

strongly adverb

with force or conviction

also strongly recommend, strongly advise, feel strongly, strongly agree, strongly disagree, earnestly, deeply (feel deeply), deeply grateful

classical

Ter. Eun. 5.8.39: vōs crēdere hoc mihi vehementer velim (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 96: vehementer ā tē dissentiō, I strongly disagree with you

vehementer

adverb

strongly, earnestly, very much

With verbs of wishing, asking, approving and disliking: vehementer rogāre, displicēre (Cicero, Lewis & Short). Of action it is “violently, fiercely” (vehementer incūsāvit, Caesar), and with an adjective simply “very” (vehementer īrāta, Plautus).

Other words

  • magnō opere (magnopere) — strongly, earnestly (wishing, urging, advising)

    adverb: the ablative of opus with magnus, written as two words or one · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 15.14.4: ego tibi Rōmam properandum magnō opere cēnseō (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 2.5: magnopere cohortātus (Lewis & Short)

    Chiefly with velle, petere, hortārī, cēnsēre: urging, advising or wishing hard. Literally “with great labour”. Lewis & Short: Plautus, Caesar and Livy write one word, Cicero’s best manuscripts two.

  • valdē — very much, strongly

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.15.2: valdē aveō scīre quid agās

    The everyday “very, very much” (see very); with a verb of wishing, “strongly, badly”.

Examples

  • vōs crēdere hoc mihi vehementer velim

    I would very much like you to believe me in thisTer. Eun. 5.8.39 (Lewis & Short)

  • ego tibi Rōmam properandum magnō opere cēnseō

    I strongly advise you to hurry to RomeCic. Fam. 15.14.4 (Lewis & Short)

  • valdē aveō scīre quid agās

    I very much want to know how you areCic. Att. 1.15.2

See also very, a lot, firmly, especially, affect.
